title: Minimum Operations to Make a Special Number
summary: Given a 0-indexed string num representing a non-negative integer, find the minimum number of deletions required to make the integer divisible by 25.
statement: Given a 0-indexed string num representing a non-negative integer, find the minimum number of deletions required to make the integer divisible by 25. An integer is divisible by 25 if its last two digits are either 00, 25, 50, or 75.
constraints: num is a nonempty decimal string without leading zeros.
Delete any digits while preserving the order of those retained; deleting all digits represents zero.
Return the fewest deletions producing a multiple of 25.
hints: A nonzero decimal multiple of 25 ends in 00, 25, 50, or 75.
Search backward for each two-digit ending and also consider retaining a single zero.
For a found pair at left<right, deletions equal digits after right plus digits between the pair.

Any retained number with at least two digits must use one of the four endings; choosing the rightmost feasible pair minimizes deletions for that ending, and the single-zero case covers all shorter results.
editorial: Any retained number with at least two digits must use one of the four endings; choosing the rightmost feasible pair minimizes deletions for that ending, and the single-zero case covers all shorter results.

tests.explanation: Keeping the suffix pattern 50 and deleting the final two digits costs two.
A best retained ending is 00 after three deletions.
